headline: Your partner got a promotion. Dinner is on them.
An old friend drops by unannounced. You talk until 3am.
A delighted client slips you a thank-you bonus you did not invoice for.
Your kid's first word was "deploy". You are not sure how to feel.
Your gym buddy drags you through a four-week streak.
You caught a cold. There are tissues in the keyboard.
Your landlord "regretfully" raises the rent. Again.
Your partner points out you have said "one sec" for six hours.
A sleepless week with the newborn. Coffee is a food group now.
A friend's wedding weekend: open bar, bad dancing, good speeches.
Family emergency. You drop everything and catch the next flight.
Parked for "just five minutes". The city disagreed.
The sushi place was not, in fact, "probably fine".
A joke about your company does numbers. Your DMs are a warzone.
Your friends throw you a surprise party. You genuinely did not see it coming.
A tax refund lands. Past-you filed something right for once.
Your upstairs neighbour takes up the drums. At night.
Your partner asks you to take one weekend off. Just one.
body: They have not asked for anything in a while, which is its own kind of asking. The sprint ends Sunday either way.

headline: Your mother needs someone to drive her to appointments for a month.
body: Your sibling cannot. She has not asked directly, which is how you know.

headline: A friend's startup wants you as an advisor, for equity in something unproven.
body: They want the name as much as the hours, and they are honest about that. The equity is worth nothing today and might stay that way.

choices.label: Say yes to two hours a month
Skip the advising and write a small cheque
Tell them you have nothing left this year
choices.detail: Free · relationships −4 · mood +2 for the honesty

headline: Your best friend's wedding lands on launch week.
body: The date was set eleven months ago. The launch date was set by you, last Tuesday.

effects.reason: A wedding you promised to attend

choices.label: Send a gift and your apologies

headline: Your kid's recital is at the same hour as a dinner you were told to attend.
body: She has practised the same eight bars every evening for a month. The dinner is the kind you get asked to once.

choices.label: Sit in the third row with a phone that stays in your pocket

headline: Your doctor uses the word "concerning" about your bloodwork.
body: Nothing urgent. Nothing to ignore either. She writes down three things and asks you to actually do them.

headline: Your landlord is selling. You have sixty days.
body: The letter is polite and final. Sixty days is plenty if you start this week and not nearly enough if you don't.

choices.label: Ask three friends and buy pizza
Pay movers and get it over with

headline: Your brother asks to borrow money and will not say what for.
body: He asked by text, at eleven at night, with the amount in it. He has never asked before.

headline: Your partner has an offer in another city and is waiting to see your face.
body: It is the job they talked about long before they met you. They have not said what they want you to say.

choices.label: Tell them to take it and work out the rest
Ask them to stay one more year

headline: The school has changed pickup to 3pm and nobody asked the parents.
body: Three o'clock is the middle of the afternoon and the middle of everything. The other parents already have a rota spreadsheet.

headline: A school reunion invitation arrives, addressed to who you used to be.
body: There is a form asking what you have been up to. You start typing and delete it four times.

choices.label: Go and answer "so what do you do" forty times

headline: A founder friend calls at midnight and does not really want advice.
body: He is talking fast about nothing in particular, which is how he does this. You have both been here before, on different ends of the phone.

headline: Your car makes the noise and then stops making any noise at all.
body: The mechanic says “at this mileage” twice, in the tone that means it. The bus goes near enough, most days.

choices.label: Sell it and take the bus

headline: Someone who loves you suggests, carefully, that you talk to somebody.
body: They have clearly been working up to saying it for a while. They also have a name and a number written down already.

headline: There is a dog at the shelter that has decided you are its person.
body: She came to the front of the pen and stayed there. The volunteer mentions, lightly, that nobody has asked about her in six weeks.

choices.label: Walk away, think about it for a year

headline: You look at your personal account and it is smaller than the company's.
body: You have been paying yourself the minimum for long enough that it stopped feeling like a decision you were making.

headline: Your family does Sunday lunch and has stopped expecting you.
body: Nobody has said anything about it, which is worse. They set the table for the number of people who usually come.

headline: Your ceiling develops an opinion about the flat upstairs.
You find the guitar behind the door. It needs new strings and forty minutes.
You have slept less than five hours for nine days and it shows in the standup.
Your partner cooked the thing you liked when you were both broke.
There is a drawing on the fridge of you, at a desk, with a laptop.
It was your birthday yesterday and you found out from a bank email.
Your neighbours invite you over and you cannot remember their names.
body: You have lived next to them for two years and exchanged nods. The invitation is handwritten and pushed under the door.

choices.label: Go, bring wine, learn the names

headline: You have been asked to give a speech and given three weeks' notice.
body: You were asked because you are the one who is good at talking to rooms. Three weeks is plenty, and three weeks vanishes.

headline: You are awake at 4am doing arithmetic about runway.
A great-aunt you met twice has left you something.
You sign up for a 10k in a moment of optimism.
body: It is eight weeks out and you were feeling good about yourself at the time. The entry fee has already left your account.

choices.label: Actually train for it
choices.detail: Health +16 · energy −4 · eight weeks of mornings

headline: Your partner has an idea and wants to know if it is any good.
body: It is not a good idea. They are not asking you as a founder.

choices.label: Ask questions instead of giving verdicts
Tell them what is wrong with it

headline: They are digging up your road for eight weeks.
Someone lists you as a reference without asking.
body: The call comes in cold, from a recruiter who assumes you are pleased to help. You remember exactly how they worked.

choices.label: Give them a glowing one anyway

headline: You are single, it is a holiday, and everyone else has plans.
body: The office is empty, the flat is quiet, and the group chat is full of other people's photographs.

choices.label: Text six people and see who answers

headline: Someone interesting matches with you and asks a real question.
body: They asked something you actually want to answer. You have been leaving messages four days out of habit rather than strategy.

headline: Your kid is up all night with a fever and the meeting is at nine.
body: By four in the morning it is a bad night rather than an emergency. The meeting was booked three weeks ago and cannot easily move twice.

choices.label: Go in on two hours of sleep

headline: The friend you get lunch with every month is moving abroad.
An estate agent sends you a listing you would have laughed at three years ago.
Your flight credit from a cancelled holiday expires in a month.
body: It is enough for five days somewhere warm, and it disappears at the end of the month whatever you do.

choices.label: Book five days somewhere with bad wifi

headline: The drummer upstairs moves out. The silence is startling.
Someone emails about code you wrote eight years ago that still runs somewhere.
The gym emails to say they miss you. You have paid them for fourteen months.
body: The email says they miss you and includes a graph of your visits. There is one bar on it, in March.

headline: Your partner asks where this is going, and means the company as much as the two of you.
body: It is not a fight. They ask it calmly, at the kitchen table, and then wait for as long as it takes.

choices.label: Give them a real answer with a date in it
choices.detail: Relationships +16 · you have to keep it

choices.label: Say it depends on the next launch

headline: Your anniversary with {partner} is this week.
body: They booked the table a month ago and have not mentioned it since, which is how you know it matters. The week is what it is.

choices.label: Take the wavering hire out instead
choices.detail: An evening · bond +10 with your unhappiest hire · affection −20

headline: Your anniversary again. You missed the last one too.
body: {partner} hasn't brought it up. That is not the same as not noticing. There is no table booked this year.

choices.label: Be there — all of it
choices.detail: An evening · affection +22 · the last miss is forgiven

choices.label: Flowers, again
choices.detail: Affection −25 · they don't say it's fine

headline: {partner} brings up the evening you didn't come to.
body: Not angrily, which is what makes it land. They ask, over the washing up, what it would take for the next one to be different.

choices.label: Take them somewhere this week
choices.detail: An evening · affection +18 · −$300 · the miss is forgiven

headline: {child}'s birthday is on Saturday.
body: They asked whether you'd be there, in the way kids ask when they already know the answer. The party is at four. The week is launch week, or it might as well be.

choices.label: Take the afternoon for the party
Send a present with a card you didn't write

headline: {child}'s birthday. You missed the last one too.
body: They didn't ask this year. There is a drawing on the fridge of everyone who was there last time; you are not in it.

choices.label: Be there, early, and stay to the end
choices.detail: An evening · relationships +16 · mood +12 · the last miss is forgiven

headline: {child} asks why you weren't at the party.
body: It comes out at bedtime, the way the real questions do. Not a complaint — a question, which is worse.

choices.label: Take a day, just the two of you
choices.detail: An evening · relationships +14 · mood +10 · the miss is forgiven

choices.label: Explain what a launch is to a six-year-old

headline: The date you gave {partner} is this week.
body: You said a date. They wrote it down. It is on the fridge, under the magnet from the launch party, and the week has arrived.

choices.label: You shipped. Take the week you promised.

headline: {partner} has stopped asking where this is going.
body: They don't mention the date any more. They have started making plans that don't have you in them, and telling you about them afterwards.

choices.label: Cancel the week and go away together

headline: The year you asked {partner} for is up.
body: They didn't set a reminder. They didn't need to. The job is still there, and so is the question, and this time they are not waiting to see your face.

choices.label: Tell them to take it — you'll make it work from here
choices.detail: Affection +20 · relationships +18 · energy −12 for the commuting

headline: {child} has stopped practising.
body: The eight bars were for you. They say they are bored of the piano now, in the voice that means something else.

choices.label: Ask them to play it for you tonight
Say you'll hear it at the weekend

headline: The fever hasn't broken. Second night.
body: The meeting went fine. Nobody at the meeting is awake at three in the morning holding a thermometer.

choices.label: Go in again
choices.detail: Energy −18 · health −6 · relationships −10 · you catch it

headline: The weekend you said you'd take after the launch.
body: The launch happened, or it didn't. Either way it is eight weeks later, and {partner} has kept count.

headline: {child} said a whole sentence today, and it was about work.
body: “Daddy is on a call” — or the local equivalent. It came out complete, in order, and slightly weary, which is the part that lands.

choices.label: Stop, write it in the notebook, stay on the floor an hour

headline: {child} starts school on Monday.
body: The uniform is too big on purpose. Drop-off is at nine, which is the hour the week gets decided in.

choices.label: Walk them in, both of you pretending not to be nervous
Let someone else take them and ask about it that evening

headline: {child}'s door has been closed for three days.
body: Not slammed. Just closed, in the way that means the house is now two houses. Kids grow up faster than companies, and this one got there first.

choices.label: Knock, sit on the floor of the hallway, wait them out
Give them space — and take the evening back

headline: {child} found a flat.
body: Two buses away, a deposit you offered to cover and they refused. The van is booked for Saturday morning.

choices.label: Drive the van yourself, carry the heavy end
Send money and a good-luck message

headline: One of your oldest friends is getting married, and the date is a Saturday.
body: The invitation has been on the fridge for a month. It is a two-hour drive, it is the whole weekend, and they asked you to say something at the dinner.

choices.label: Send the gift and your apologies

headline: A friend quit their job and started something of their own.
A friend has stopped answering anybody, including you.
body: Three unread messages and a voicemail. You know exactly what this is, because you were here eighteen months ago and somebody drove over.

headline: A friend is taking a job on the other side of the world.
Somebody repeated what you said. Word for word.
You have a reputation now: the founder who says the thing out loud.
Somebody you were decent to once called for no reason at all.
A screenshot of you is doing the rounds of a group chat you're not in.
Your calendar has four coffees in it and all four are apologies.
body: Four people, four flat whites, four versions of the same sentence. You could do them all this week, or you could do the one that matters.

headline: Somebody has stopped replying, and you know exactly which somebody.
You were the anecdote at a dinner you weren't invited to.
"Difficult but effective" is now a thing recruiters say about you.
Three in the morning, and you are replaying a sentence from March.
Somebody forgave you before you got round to asking.
You have got very good at which phone is face-down.
You rehearsed a sentence in the car before going in.
A friend asked one very carefully worded question.
body: They didn't accuse you of anything. They asked whether everything was alright at home, and then they waited longer than people usually wait.

headline: Two calendars, one Thursday, and somebody's assistant does admin properly.
A receipt turned up in a coat pocket. It was a good restaurant.
A newsletter called it a feud. You'd been calling it a difference of opinion.
They were at the same conference. Same room, twice.
body: You were four metres apart at the coffee table for a full minute. Somebody was filming the room on their phone.

headline: They hired somebody who used to sit six feet from you.
Your nemesis said something genuinely complimentary in public.
You both know the same person and that person is exhausted.
There is a chair in the kitchen that nobody sits in now.
A letter arrived. Handwritten, which nobody does any more.
body: Two pages, both sides, no return address. It doesn't ask you for anything, which is the part that's hard to put down.

headline: Somebody rang for a reference on a person you fired with cause.
There was a wedding. You found out from a photo.
"How are things with them?" asked somebody who hadn't heard.
A photo from four years ago came up on your phone this morning.
Somebody asked you how to handle a person. Genuinely asked.
A favour you did without thinking came back with interest.
Somebody defended you in a room you weren't in.
You could not remember the name of somebody who remembered yours.
Somebody quoted you to you, and you did not recognise it.
An evening with people, and nobody wanted anything from you.
You wrote a list of everyone you owe a call. It got long.
body: Fourteen names. Some of them have been on the list since the seed round. The list is not the hard part.

headline: Somebody recognised you in a queue and could not place you.
body: They knew the face and not the name, worked through three wrong guesses out loud, and settled on “you do something with computers”. Which is accurate.

headline: You have acquired a reply guy.
body: Under every post, within four minutes, a man who disagrees. He has been doing this for eleven weeks. You have started checking for him.

headline: Your mother has found the feed.
body: She has liked every post going back nine months and left one comment, on the angriest of them, that says “very good”.

headline: A post of yours is in somebody's group chat, and not kindly.
body: A friend forwards it with no message. Just the screenshot and the seventeen replies under it, all from people you have never met.

headline: A newsletter quoted you without asking.
body: Sixteen thousand subscribers, your sentence, and a paragraph explaining what you meant that is not what you meant.

headline: An old teacher emailed to say they always knew.
body: They did not always know. You have the report cards. But it is a kind lie and it arrived on a bad Tuesday.

headline: Somebody on the team reads everything you post and has never said so.
body: It comes out in a standup, sideways, as a joke about a take you had forgotten. The room laughs. You do not.

headline: The algorithm has gone off you.
body: Same posts, same hours, a tenth of the reach. There is nobody to appeal to. There has never been anybody to appeal to.

headline: A podcast wants ninety minutes about the early days.
body: Two microphones, one host who has read everything, and a running time nobody will finish.

headline: Your messages are now a slush pile.
body: Forty unread. Nine decks, six job applications, one man who wants you to look at his cousin's app, and somebody's actual emergency, buried.

headline: There is a parody account of you now.
body: Same photo, one letter different, and it is funnier than you are. It has more followers than the company does.

choices.label: Report it
choices.detail: Free · mood −5 · they screenshot the report

headline: You spent a conference in a hallway you could not leave.
body: Six conversations, none finished, and a talk you paid to attend and did not see a slide of.

headline: Three recruiters used your feed as a directory.
body: Every engineer you have publicly thanked got a call this week. Public gratitude, it turns out, is a hiring list.

headline: Somebody offered to post for you.
body: Four figures a month, your voice, their hours. They sent samples. Two of them are better than anything you have written.

headline: Somebody worked out which coffee shop.
body: Not a threat. A photograph of your usual table, posted, with the time. You have started going somewhere else, which is its own small loss.

headline: Your partner is tired of being in the photographs.
body: They never asked for an audience and they married a company, not a channel. It is said once, calmly, over dinner.

headline: You got ratioed by an account with a cartoon frog.
body: Eleven likes on yours. Four thousand on theirs. The frog is right, which is the worst part.

headline: A publisher wants the book.
body: Advance up front, manuscript in a year, a title they have already chosen that you would not have chosen. It is not a lot of money and it is a great deal of evenings.

choices.label: Sign it
choices.detail: +$18,000 to the wallet · an evening · energy −10

headline: A magazine is writing a profile, and it has a photographer.
body: They want a day, the office, and one honest sentence about the hardest month. Two of those are easy.

headline: You are on a shortlist for something with a trophy.
body: Founder of the year, regional, sponsored by a bank. Four nominees, one table, a dinner you pay for.

headline: An open letter about the industry wants your signature.
body: Two hundred names already. You agree with about eighty per cent of it, which is either enough or exactly the problem.

headline: An investor opened a meeting by quoting you back at yourself.
body: They had the post printed. Underlined. It was a joke when you wrote it, and it is a thesis now.

headline: You read your own press and did not recognise the person in it.
body: Visionary, apparently. Relentless. The person in the photograph has not slept properly since March and cannot remember their own passwords.

headline: The team read your interview before you told them about it.
body: One sentence about the next twelve months that you have not said in the building. It was true. It was just not theirs yet.

headline: Two people are waiting outside the office to meet you.
body: Students, polite, one with a printout. They have been there since ten. Reception does not know what the policy is because there is no policy.

headline: A take you posted at midnight is being discussed on three continents.
body: It was a shower thought with a typo in it. It now has a defender in Berlin and a detractor in Seoul.

headline: A conference wants the keynote. Unpaid, honoured.
body: Two thousand seats, twenty-five minutes, and the words “we cannot pay speakers but the exposure is enormous”, which you have now heard from both sides.

headline: A former colleague wrote a thread about what you were like to work for.
body: Nine posts. Two of them are unfair. Six of them are fair. The seventh you have thought about every day since.

headline: Somebody is running a giveaway in your name.
body: Your photo, your handle with a hyphen in it, and a wallet address. Four people have already sent money and one of them has emailed you about it.

headline: A photographer followed you to the school gate.
body: Nothing was published. That is not the point and everybody at home knows it is not the point.

headline: Nine companies would like you on their advisory board.
body: Equity, a quarterly call, and your name on their site, which is the only part any of them actually want.

headline: You have started drafting posts and deleting them.
body: Eleven drafts this week. Not one of them was wrong. Every one of them could be read badly by somebody who wanted to.

headline: A documentary crew would like six months of access.
body: They want the good quarter and they will take whichever one they get. Nobody has ever regretted saying no to this.

headline: Television wants seven minutes on the morning sofa.
body: A car at half past five, a green room with one banana in it, and a host who will ask whether robots are coming for our jobs.

headline: Someone made a very bad portrait of you and it is going around.
body: Oil on canvas, three feet tall, the eyes not quite level. It is in a gallery. It is selling.

headline: A talk show wants you and a rival on the same sofa.
body: They have pitched it as a conversation. It is not a conversation. Everyone involved knows what it is.

choices.label: Take the sofa
choices.detail: Reputation −2 · mood −4 · the clip lives for ever

headline: You cannot buy milk without a conversation about the company.
body: Nobody is unkind. Everybody has a question. You have started going to the shop at eleven at night, which the doctor would have opinions about.

headline: A charity would like your name and, ideally, your money.
body: It is a good cause. So were the other four this month. There is no formula for this and everybody pretends there is.

headline: Somebody is writing a book about you without asking.
body: They have interviewed nine former employees and two people you went to school with. You are not going to enjoy the chapter about year two.

headline: Your partner reads about it before you tell them.
body: They do not shout. They put the phone face down on the table and wait.

headline: You are awake at four again, doing arithmetic you already did at two.
Your mother has seen something and would like it explained slowly.
body: She is not angry. That is much worse and she knows it.

headline: An old friend texts: 'tell me it isn't the thing I think it is'.
The first legal bill arrives, itemised by the six-minute unit.
body: Somebody billed you for reading the letter that said how much they bill.

headline: A neighbour asks, over the bins, whether you are 'the one from the news'.
Somebody at the school gate stops talking when you arrive.
You have started going to the gym at half past five to avoid people.
You dream about the courtroom. In the dream you are also the prosecutor.
Your partner's friend, who is a solicitor, offers to look at the papers for free.
body: They read for forty minutes and say 'right' twice.

headline: One of your children asks whether you are going to prison.
body: They ask it the way they ask about weather.

headline: You have a drink after the meeting, and then the second one is not after anything.
An anonymous letter arrives at the house, not the office.
body: That is the detail you keep coming back to. The house.

headline: You walk eleven kilometres without deciding to.
Nobody mentions it, all week, at all, by anybody, once.
body: It is the loudest week you have had.

headline: A parking ticket, for a bay you have paid for since March.
Somebody took the wing mirror off in the night and left the rest.
The service light comes on, and it is not the kind you can ignore.
body: The garage can fit you in Thursday. Thursday is the board meeting, which the garage does not know.

headline: The valet at the venue recognises the car before he recognises you.
A camera on the ring road has your number plate and an opinion.
Somebody at the office asks what you paid for it. You round down.
You take the long way home for no reason and arrive in a better mood.
Dead battery on a Monday. Everything about that sentence is true.
The tenant's rent is nine days late and their phone goes to voicemail.
body: They have never been late before. There is a version of this where you are the villain and a version where you are $520 down.

headline: The boiler in the flat has gone. In February, obviously.
A letter from an agent says the flat is worth more than you paid.
You go to the cabin for two nights and answer nothing.
A neighbour has written to you about a hedge. Two pages, both sides.
Whatever kind of day it was, something was waiting by the door.
The animal walks across the keyboard mid-board-call. Nobody minds.
Something has been chewed. It was expensive and it was yours.
You take it out at six and the street is empty and the air is cold.
The vet says the words 'we'll keep an eye on it', which do not help.
body: Nothing is wrong. Nothing is confirmed to be right, either. She wants to see it again in a month.

headline: You screenshot the number at its high and send it to nobody.
It moved thirty per cent overnight. You are not sure which way yet.
Somebody at a party asks you what to buy. You tell them not to.
The casino sends a car. That is how they say they know your name.
body: A room, a dinner, and a marker if you want one. They have done the arithmetic on you and it came out in their favour.

choices.label: Take the dinner, skip the tables

headline: Four numbers. The fifth one was on the ticket you did not buy.
A trade site prints an estimate of what you are worth. It is wrong.
Your insurer would like to review everything you own. All of it.
The one after the launch turns into the four after the launch.
You have had three coffees and it is not yet ten in the morning.
You checked it under the table at dinner and everyone saw you.
It is ten past two and you are still holding the phone.
You count the units for the week and then stop counting them.
body: The number was not catastrophic. It was just higher than the number you would have said out loud if somebody had asked.

headline: You put a receipt in your own pocket rather than the shared drawer.
They ask, kindly, and you answer the question they did not ask.
Somebody on the team makes a joke about it and nobody laughs.
A week goes by where you did not think about it once.
You have replaced it with running, which is its own kind of odd.
There is a room above a pub on Tuesdays. You have the address.
body: Nobody there is famous and nobody there cares that you are. That is most of the point of it.

headline: You are back where you were in March and nobody has noticed yet.
Your doctor mentions it before you do, which is the awkward order.
The sleep clinic can see you in six weeks. You write it down.
A prescription, a leaflet, and a sentence about 'lifestyle factors'.
You get a second opinion. It is the same opinion, said more slowly.
A photo from three years ago comes up. You look at it for a while.
You walked past the place tonight and kept walking.
You lay awake doing arithmetic you already know the answer to.
Your partner asked where the money came from, in the kitchen, not looking at you.
body: They have asked once before and let it go. They are not going to let it go twice.

choices.label: Say it's a family office
choices.detail: Free · which is true, and is not an answer

headline: Your partner has read something about your investors that you did not tell them.
You changed the locks at home, and did not say why.
You took a different route home for the fourth night running.
A friend has stopped replying, and you know exactly which week it started.
You have been invited to dinner by people you would rather not eat with.
body: It is not phrased as an invitation and there is a car coming at eight.

choices.label: Go to the dinner
choices.detail: An evening · it is a good restaurant and a long night

choices.label: Send an excuse
choices.detail: Free · the excuse is accepted, and filed

headline: One of the children asked why a man was outside the school.
You paid for a round in cash and enjoyed it more than you should have.
You spent an hour at home feeding paper into a shredder you bought for this.
You slept eight hours for the first time since the wire cleared.
You spent the day in a room with two officers and a jug of water.
You changed your number and gave it to eleven people.
You caught yourself whistling on the way in, which has not happened for a while.
There are two toothbrushes in the bathroom and one of them is new.
You have been in the spare room eleven days. Nobody has said so out loud.
A leaflet appears on the counter. It is not addressed to anybody.
body: It is for a place on the high street with a sofa in the photograph. It has been there two days and neither of you has moved it.

choices.label: After the quarter
choices.detail: Affection −10 · the leaflet stays where it is

headline: Your friends have started answering slower. They have been asked to pick a side.
You were removed from a group chat named after a holiday you all took.
Your eldest asked why you sleep with the door shut now.
The forms arrive as a PDF with somebody else's initials on every page.
Half the bookshelf is gone and the half that is left leans.
You drove to the old supermarket on autopilot and sat in the car park a while.
Their solicitor calls the office line, which somebody answers cheerfully.
body: They want the cabin question settled by Friday. Your CFO is standing in the doorway holding a payroll run and pretending to read it.

choices.label: Tell them to put it in writing

headline: The first handover is in a retail park because it is exactly halfway.
You found the ring in a drawer, in an envelope, in a box, which is three decisions.
A journalist asks, on the record, whether the divorce affected the roadmap.
